_comment: DEV-ONLY eval set for listing semantic search. NOT used by the app/production.
Each entry: { query, expected_listing_ids, notes }.
- query: a natural-language search a parent/athlete might type.
- expected_listing_ids: the program (listing) UUIDs that SHOULD rank in the
top results for this query. Fill these from real rows: in Supabase run
`select id, title, sport_type, skill_level, age_group from programs;` and
paste the ids that genuinely match the query. Leave [] if not yet labeled
(the eval scores recall only over queries that have expected ids).
HOW TO GROW TO 50 LABELED QUERIES:
1. Pull the full listing catalog (query above). Skim titles/descriptions.
2. For each distinct sport + skill_level + age_group cluster, write 2-3
realistic queries (a beginner phrasing, an intent phrasing, a location-free
paraphrase). Vary vocabulary so it isn't keyword-matchable.
3. Label each with the 1-5 listing ids a human would consider correct.
4. Keep a few HARD negatives (queries whose best match is subtle) and a few
EASY ones (exact-topic) so recall@10 spreads out and is diagnostic.
5. NEVER label on price/location/availability/certs/background-check — those
are structured/deterministic, not semantic (hard rule). Label on the
descriptive content only (sport, skill, age, what's included).
6. Aim for ~50 across the sports you actually list; re-run run_eval.py and
watch recall@10 / mean rank as you tune embeddings + (later) hybrid search.
